instructions: At least 2 hours ahead, and up to 3: grind the black and white peppercorns coarsely. Chop the stems and roots of the cilantro (about 3 tbsp) and pound them with the garlic and peppercorns into a rough paste. Stir the paste in a large bowl with the light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, sugar and 1 tsp of the salt until the sugar dissolves. Add the wings, toss to coat, cover and chill.

Slice the shallots thin and evenly. Rinse the rice in a strainer, put it in a saucepan with 2 1/4 cups water, bring it to a boil, cover, turn the heat to low and cook for 15 minutes. Let it sit covered.

Pour the oil into a heavy pot at least 4 inches deep. Heat it over medium heat to 250°F, or until a shallot slice sizzles gently. Add the shallots and fry for 2 to 3 minutes, stirring, until golden. Lift them out with a slotted spoon onto paper towels. They crisp as they cool.
Turn the heat up to medium-high and bring the oil to 350°F. Without a thermometer, drop in a pinch of flour. It should sizzle right away.
Mix the rice flour into the wings and marinade by hand, a little at a time, with about 1/2 cup water, until it makes a batter as thick as pancake batter that clings to the wings.

Fry the wings in two batches, about 8 wings at a time, for 8 minutes each, turning now and then, until the coating is deep golden brown. Stand back a little. They'll spatter. Check the oil comes back to 350°F between batches.
You're cooking the wings to 175°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check one there. No thermometer? Cut into the thickest wing: it's done when there's no pink left.
Transfer the wings to a rack set over a baking sheet and let them rest for 10 minutes. Keep the first batch warm in a 200°F oven.
Taste a wing. If it's flat, sprinkle the rest with a pinch more salt, using the remaining 1/4 tsp.
Pile the wings on a platter and scatter the fried shallots over the top. Serve with the rice and the sweet chili sauce in a small bowl.
advance_prep_notes: marinate the wings 2 to 3 hours ahead
method_notes: Thai Cookbook leads (4.5 from 6,266 ratings): a coriander root, garlic and peppercorn marinade with soy sauces and sugar, a rice flour batter and a deep fry of wings, topped with crisp fried shallots. Hungry in Thailand (5 from 5 votes) agrees on the spice paste and fried shallots and suggests sweet chili sauce. Jasmine rice replaces the soaked and steamed sticky rice to keep it a weeknight dinner, and the wing count is for a 4-person table.
